title: James Marsden Says Avengers: Doomsday Will Showcase Cyclops as a Leader
excerpt:
James Marsden wants his return as Scott Summers to be meaningful.
The Russo brothers are emphasizing Cyclops' leadership qualities.
body_md:
One recurring criticism of the Fox-era X-Men movies concerns their treatment of Scott Summers. Despite casting James Marsden, the films frequently placed Cyclops in Wolverine's shadow, with his relationship with Jean Grey and rivalry with Wolverine taking precedence over his position as a team leader. That approach differed from the character familiar to readers of the comics and viewers of the animated series.

Speaking to Sharp Magazine, Marsden discussed conversations with Marvel Studios and directors Joe and Anthony Russo about taking a more authentic approach to Cyclops. The actor acknowledged the limited screen time available in a film featuring so many characters, while stressing that his return needed to serve a meaningful purpose.

Marsden did not want another brief appearance driven solely by nostalgia. Having already returned for a cameo at the end of X-Men: Days of Future Past, he wanted this opportunity to explore what Scott Summers brings to the team. He expressed satisfaction with the result without revealing plot details.

The final Avengers: Doomsday trailer offers an indication of that direction. Cyclops is shown fighting Sam Wilson before delivering his signature line, To me, my X-Men, as other heroes arrive alongside him. The scene highlights his leadership, although it does not establish how extensive his role will be in the finished film.

The animated X-Men '97 has recently demonstrated how compelling Scott Summers can be when his leadership is central to the story. Bringing that quality to the live-action films could address longstanding criticism and establish a useful foundation for the X-Men's future within Marvel's cinematic universe.

Doomsday also faces the challenge of introducing Doctor Doom, balancing an enormous ensemble and establishing the next stage of the story ahead of Secret Wars. Marsden's comments confirm the creative intention behind his return, rather than specific plot developments or the amount of screen time Cyclops will receive.
